text: Reproduce the square-rectangle substitution violation. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class Rect { protected int w, h;
@Override void setHeight(int x) { this.w = x; this.h = x; } }
public static void main(String[] args) { resize(new Rect()); resize(new Sq()); }
explanation: Verified: `expected 20, got 20` then `expected 20, got 25`. Nobody made a mistake in the ordinary sense — `resize` reasons correctly from `Rect` and `Sq` maintains its own invariant honestly. The mistake was the word `extends`, which promised substitutability that cannot hold, because `Rect` carries an unwritten guarantee that setting the height leaves the width alone.
